title: Cancel tickets and release holds at the repair shop

blocks.text: A repair shop keeps a wait list of numbered tickets, served in the order customers joined, and puts holds on accounts with unpaid bills. The front desk has two complaints: when a customer leaves, sometimes someone else's ticket disappears, and a released hold stays on the account.

Finish `cancel(int ticket)` and `release(int accountId)` in `src/main/java/practice/WaitList.java`. `cancel` takes that customer's ticket off the list and keeps everyone else in order; `release` lifts the hold on that account. About two lines in total.

cases.says: cancelling the ticket at the front of the list leaves the others in order
releasing an account that has no hold leaves the other holds in place
cancel takes off the ticket with that number, not the ticket at that position
release given an int account id lifts the hold on that account

origin.section: On a List of Integers, remove(int) Takes an Index, Not a Value

concepts: Removing an int from a collection keyed by Long boxes it to an Integer, which never equals a Long, so nothing is removed.
On a List<Integer>, remove with an int argument removes by index; removing a value needs an Integer argument.
